intro: All four join a condition A to a result B, and all four can be translated "if" or "when". What differs is the link between A and B. と: B follows A automatically, every time. ば: A is the condition B depends on ("as long as A"). たら: once A has happened, B; the all-purpose "if / when". なら: "if that is the case": A is taken as given, often from what someone just said, and B is your comment on it.

skills.rule: Plain non-past + と: whenever A happens, B follows as a matter of course, and B is never a request, wish or plan.
skills.explain:
と attaches to the dictionary form or the ない-form, never to the past: 押すと, 行かないと, 安いと, 静かだと, 雨だと. The tense of the whole sentence is carried by the last verb.

と states a fixed link that the speaker has no say in: machines (このボタンを押すと), nature (春になると), habits (父は飲むとすぐ寝る) and directions (角を曲がると、駅があります).

That is its hard edge: the main clause cannot be a request, command, invitation, wish or decision. 駅に着くと電話してください is wrong; use たら. With a past main clause, と reports what you found or what happened next in a story: 外に出ると、雨が降っていた "when I went outside, it was raining".
patterns: [verb dictionary form] と、[discovery in the past]

examples.jp: 春[はる]になる{と}、暖[あたた]かくなります。
examples.en: When spring comes, it gets warm.

examples.jp: このボタンを押[お]す{と}、お湯[ゆ]が出[で]ます。
examples.en: If you press this button, hot water comes out.

examples.jp: まっすぐ行[い]く{と}、右[みぎ]に銀行[ぎんこう]があります。
examples.en: If you go straight on, there's a bank on the right.

examples.jp: 父[ちち]はお酒[さけ]を飲[の]む{と}、すぐ寝[ね]てしまいます。
examples.en: Whenever my father drinks, he falls asleep right away.

examples.jp: 窓[まど]を開[あ]ける{と}、外[そと]は雪[ゆき]だった。
examples.en: When I opened the window, it was snowing outside.

contrast.note: たら also means "when / if" and can be followed by a request or plan: 着いたら電話して. Choose と only when B is an automatic or habitual outcome.
For general truths ば is also correct (押せば開く). ば puts the weight on the condition ("as long as you press"); と simply links cause and outcome.
ても is the opposite link: "even if". 押すと開く "press it and it opens"; 押しても開かない "even if you press it, it won't open".

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]に着[つ]く{と}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]に着[つ]い{たら}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.note: と cannot be followed by a request. Use たら.

mistakes.bad: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]った{と}、道[みち]が滑[すべ]りやすくなります。
mistakes.good: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]る{と}、道[みち]が滑[すべ]りやすくなります。
mistakes.note: と never follows the past form: 降ると, not 降ったと. The last verb carries the tense.

skills.tip: Can you add "every time, automatically"? Then と. Is the second half a request or a plan? Then not と.

skills.rule: The ば-form says "if A holds, B": it singles out A as the condition that B depends on.
skills.explain:
Forms: godan verbs change the final -u to -e + ば (行けば, 飲めば, あれば); ichidan verbs take れば (食べれば); する → すれば, 来る → 来れば; い-adjectives take ければ (安ければ, and いい → よければ); ない → なければ. Nouns and na-adjectives use であれば, or more often なら.

ば focuses on what it takes: "as long as A", "all you need is A". It is the form of advice and regret: 薬を飲めばよくなる, どうすればいいですか, 聞けばよかった "I should have asked". ～ば～ほど means "the more ..., the more ...".

The edge: if the ば-clause is your listener's or your own action, the main clause cannot be a request, invitation or intention: say 着いたら電話して, not 着けば. (Someone else's action is fine: 君が行けば僕も行く.) If A is a state (ある, いる, できる, an adjective, a negative), requests are fine: 時間があれば来てください. With a past main clause, ば usually describes what did not happen: 早く出れば間に合ったのに.

examples.jp: 安[やす]けれ{ば}、買[か]います。
examples.en: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

examples.jp: 時間[じかん]があれ{ば}、手伝[てつだ]ってください。
examples.en: If you have time, please help.

examples.jp: この薬[くすり]を飲[の]め{ば}、熱[ねつ]が下[さ]がりますよ。
examples.en: If you take this medicine, your fever will go down.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]へはどう行[い]け{ば}いいですか。
examples.en: How do I get to the station?

examples.jp: もっと勉強[べんきょう]すれ{ば}よかった。
examples.en: I should have studied more.

examples.jp: 練習[れんしゅう]すれ{ば}するほど上手[じょうず]になります。
examples.en: The more you practise, the better you get.

contrast.note: In conversation たら can replace most ば. It must replace it when an action is followed by a request or plan: 着いたら電話して, not 着けば.
なら reacts to a premise already on the table ("if you're going, then ..."). ば asks what condition brings B about. Nouns take なら, not ば.

mistakes.bad: 安[やす]いれ{ば}、買[か]います。
mistakes.good: 安[やす]けれ{ば}、買[か]います。
mistakes.note: An い-adjective drops い and adds ければ.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]に着[つ]け{ば}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]に着[つ]い{たら}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.note: After an action in the ば-clause, a request sounds wrong. Use たら.

mistakes.bad: 学生[がくせい]{ば}、安[やす]くなります。
mistakes.good: 学生[がくせい]{なら}、安[やす]くなります。
mistakes.note: A noun cannot take ば directly. Use なら (or であれば).

skills.tip: Think "as long as A" or "all it takes is A". Before a request, check that A is a state; if it is an action, switch to たら.

skills.rule: Plain past + ら: once A has happened, B; the all-purpose "if" and "when".
skills.explain:
Make the plain past and add ら: 行ったら, 食べたら, 来たら, 安かったら, 暇だったら, 雨だったら, 行かなかったら. The past form does not mean past time; it means A is complete before B starts.

たら covers "if" (雨だったら行きません) and "when" for something sure to happen (家に着いたら電話します). Unlike と, and unlike ば after an action, it freely takes any main clause: requests, invitations, wishes, decisions. In conversation it is the safe default.

With a past main clause, B is something you found or that happened outside your control: 箱を開けたら、空だった "when I opened the box, it was empty". It cannot narrate your own next deliberate act: "I got home and did my homework" is 帰ってから宿題をしました. And because A must come first, "if you're going to Kyoto, take the shinkansen" needs なら, not 行ったら.

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]だっ{たら}、行[い]きません。
examples.en: If it rains, I won't go.

examples.jp: 家[いえ]に着[つ]い{たら}、電話[でんわ]してください。
examples.en: Please call me when you get home.

examples.jp: 暇[ひま]だっ{たら}、一緒[いっしょ]に映画[えいが]を見[み]ませんか。
examples.en: If you're free, would you like to see a film together?

examples.jp: 読[よ]み終[お]わっ{たら}、貸[か]してください。
examples.en: When you've finished reading it, please lend it to me.

examples.jp: 宝[たから]くじが当[あ]たっ{たら}、何[なに]をしますか。
examples.en: What would you do if you won the lottery?

examples.jp: 箱[はこ]を開[あ]け{たら}、中[なか]は空[から]だった。
examples.en: When I opened the box, it was empty.

contrast.note: と cannot take a request or plan; たら can. For machines and nature both work, but と sounds more like a fixed rule.
たら: B happens after A. なら: B can come first. 日本に行ったら買う is "buy it there"; 日本に行くなら買う is "buy it before the trip".
For your own actions in sequence in the past, use て or てから. A past main clause after たら means B was a discovery or not your doing.

mistakes.bad: 家[いえ]に帰[かえ]っ{たら}、宿題[しゅくだい]をしました。
mistakes.good: 家[いえ]に帰[かえ]っ{てから}、宿題[しゅくだい]をしました。
mistakes.note: たら plus a past main clause implies something unexpected. For your own next action, use てから.

mistakes.bad: 京都[きょうと]へ行[い]っ{たら}、新幹線[しんかんせん]が便利[べんり]ですよ。
mistakes.good: 京都[きょうと]へ行[い]く{なら}、新幹線[しんかんせん]が便利[べんり]ですよ。
mistakes.note: The shinkansen is how you get there, so B comes before A. Use なら.

mistakes.bad: 安[やす]い{たら}、買[か]います。
mistakes.good: 安[やす]かっ{たら}、買[か]います。
mistakes.note: たら attaches to the plain past: 安い → 安かった → 安かったら.

skills.tip: Can you say "once A has happened, then B"? たら fits. If B has to happen first, use なら.

skills.rule: Noun or plain form + なら: "if that is the case"; take A as given, often from what someone just said, and say what follows.
skills.explain:
なら attaches directly to nouns and na-adjective stems (雨なら, 静かなら, 学生なら) and to plain verb and い-adjective forms (行くなら, 行ったなら, 高いなら). No だ goes in front of it: 雨なら, not 雨だなら.

なら picks up a topic or a supposition and gives advice, an opinion or a decision about it. 「カメラを買いたい」「カメラなら、あの店が安いよ」. After a noun it often means "if it's X you're talking about".

Unlike the other three, なら imposes no time order. 日本へ行くなら、円に両替しておいたほうがいい: change money before you go. 行ったら would mean once you are there. なら is not for automatic or general results: "when spring comes, the cherry trees bloom" is 春になると, never 春になるなら. In speech you will also hear のなら and んなら with the same meaning.
patterns: [plain verb / い-adjective] なら、[comment or advice]

examples.jp: 寿司[すし]{なら}、駅前[えきまえ]の店[みせ]がおいしいですよ。
examples.en: If it's sushi you want, the place by the station is good.

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]{なら}、試合[しあい]は中止[ちゅうし]です。
examples.en: If it rains, the match is off.

examples.jp: 疲[つか]れている{なら}、早[はや]く寝[ね]たほうがいいよ。
examples.en: If you're tired, you should go to bed early.

examples.jp: 山[やま]に行[い]く{なら}、暖[あたた]かい服[ふく]を持[も]って行[い]ってね。
examples.en: If you're going to the mountains, take warm clothes.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]へ行[い]く{なら}、円[えん]に両替[りょうがえ]しておいたほうがいいです。
examples.en: If you're going to Japan, you should change money into yen first.

contrast.note: たら needs A to happen first. なら does not: 行くなら傘を持って行って means take the umbrella with you from the start.
ば states the condition that brings B about (薬を飲めば治る). なら takes A as a given premise and comments on it (薬を飲むなら、食後にしてね).

mistakes.bad: 雨[あめ]だ{なら}、行[い]きません。
mistakes.good: 雨[あめ]{なら}、行[い]きません。
mistakes.note: なら follows a noun directly, with no だ.

mistakes.bad: 春[はる]になる{なら}、桜[さくら]が咲[さ]きます。
mistakes.good: 春[はる]になる{と}、桜[さくら]が咲[さ]きます。
mistakes.note: An automatic seasonal result takes と, not なら.

mistakes.bad: 日本[にほん]に着[つ]く{なら}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.good: 日本[にほん]に着[つ]い{たら}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.note: The call comes after arriving, so use たら. なら would ask for the call before you land.

skills.tip: Can you begin with "if that's the case" or "if it's X you mean"? なら. It is the only one where B can happen before A.

skills.rule: Ask in order: B before A, or reacting to a given topic? なら. B a request, wish or plan? たら. Automatic result? と. Advice or regret with いい / よかった? ば. Otherwise たら.
skills.explain:
Q1. Does B happen before A, or are you reacting to a topic someone has raised? なら: 行くなら傘を持って行って, 寿司なら駅前の店.

Q2. Is B a request, invitation, wish or decision? たら: 着いたら電話して. と is impossible here, and ば works only if A is a state: 時間があれば来て.

Q3. Is B an automatic or repeated result (machines, nature, habits, directions)? と: 押すとお湯が出る. ば and たら are also correct; と sounds most like a fixed rule.

Q4. Advice or regret with いい / よかった, or ～ば～ほど? ば: どうすればいい, 聞けばよかった.

Q5. Is B in the past? A discovery or surprise takes たら or と: 開けたら空だった. Your own next deliberate act takes none of them: use て or てから.

Otherwise, たら: it is the default in conversation.
patterns: B before A / given topic → なら
いい / よかった / ほど → ば

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]へ行[い]く{なら}、カメラを買[か]います。
examples.en: If I'm going to Japan, I'll buy a camera (before I go).

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]へ行[い]っ{たら}、カメラを買[か]います。
examples.en: When I get to Japan, I'll buy a camera (there).

examples.jp: 春[はる]になる{と}、桜[さくら]が咲[さ]きます。
examples.en: When spring comes, the cherry trees bloom.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]に着[つ]い{たら}、電話[でんわ]してください。
examples.en: Please call me when you get to the station.

examples.jp: どうすれ{ば}いいですか。
examples.en: What should I do?

examples.jp: ドアを開[あ]け{たら}、猫[ねこ]がいた。
examples.en: When I opened the door, there was a cat.

contrast.note: Both can describe an automatic result, but only たら can be followed by a request, wish or plan.
Both mean "if"; after an action, only たら can be followed by a request. ば owns いい / よかった advice and regret.
たら: A first, then B. なら: B may come first, and A is a premise taken from the context.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]に着[つ]く{と}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]に着[つ]い{たら}、電話[でんわ]してください。
mistakes.note: A request cannot follow と. Use たら.

mistakes.bad: 「パソコンを買[か]いたい。」「パソコンを買[か]っ{たら}、秋葉原[あきはばら]がいいよ。」
mistakes.good: 「パソコンを買[か]いたい。」「パソコンを買[か]う{なら}、秋葉原[あきはばら]がいいよ。」
mistakes.note: You are reacting to the other person's plan, and the shop comes before the purchase: なら.

skills.tip: Does B come first or answer a given topic? なら. Is B a request? たら. Otherwise ask whether B is automatic (と) or advice (ば), and fall back on たら.
